message.content: The sea typically looks blue—especially when it’s clear and calm. That blue hue comes from the way water absorbs and scatters sunlight: it absorbs longer wavelengths (reds, oranges) more strongly than shorter wavelengths (blues), so the reflected light we see is predominantly blue. In practice, the sea’s color can shift depending on depth, weather, and what’s floating in or beneath it—ranging from turquoise near shorelines to deep indigo in deeper waters, and even greenish or grayish tones when algae, sediment, or clouds influence the view.
